name: Tangier Beach
hero_subtitle: Municipal beach along the bay — an easy sea break from the medina hills.

overview.title: Bay Sand Below the City
overview.p1: Tangier Beach is the straightforward sandy strip along the bay. It will not compete with Agadir for resort polish, and it is not a wild Atlantic surf beach. It is where you go when the medina slopes have been enough and you want the horizon without a drive to Cap Spartel.
overview.p2: Weekends draw local families. Weekday mornings are calmer. The corniche above gives you cafés and a place to sit when the wind picks up.
overview.p3: Swim only where it looks supervised and sensible; currents and water quality can vary — follow local practice.

q1.question: Is it clean enough to swim?
q1.answer: Conditions vary — watch locals and any flags; when in doubt, walk and don’t swim.

q2.question: Facilities?
q2.answer: Seasonal loungers and cafés appear along sections of the strip.

q3.question: How far from the medina?
q3.answer: A short taxi or a longer walk depending on where you stay.

q4.question: Do I need a guide at Tangier Beach?
q4.answer: Optional for a simple visit; useful for historical context.

q5.question: Is Tangier Beach suitable for families?
q5.answer: Yes with normal supervision on steps, cliffs or wet stone.

food.title: Corniche and beach cafés
food.p1: Cafés along the front cover drinks and light meals; serious fish is often better nearer the port restaurants.
food.p2: Beach menus are convenient; port kitchens often win on freshness.
